description:
Found by the cold review of fz-5xp.31. PRE-EXISTING.

    fn main(), do: dbg(7.5 % 2.0)

  interp -> 1.5
  run    -> abort in fz_dynamic_float_arith_unsupported (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs)
  build  -> the same

CAUSE. `lower_arith_binop` (src/compiler2/native_codegen/prim.rs) excludes
`BinOp::Mod` from BOTH float paths, and the tagged fallback has no float arm, so
the call reaches the runtime's "unsupported" trap.

SHARPLY RELEVANT: the `fz_op_rem_ff` / `fz_op_rem_fi` / `fz_op_rem_if` shims
that fz-5xp.31 rewrote implement float `%` CORRECTLY. `Kernel` declares all
three. So the operator is fully specified and implemented on one door and
missing on two -- the interpreter is currently the only door that can evaluate
it at all.

Related: fz-5xp.6 (Elixir division semantics) touches the same lowering, and
Elixir's own `rem/2` is integer-only while `%` here is not. Settle what fz's `%`
means for floats as part of that, then make all three doors do it.

DONE = float `%` agrees on all three doors, or is refused on all three with one
diagnostic. Not one door answering and two aborting.
title: [BUG] Float remainder aborts run and build
